recipes.name: Quick Fish Tacos
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 pound tilapia fillets, cut into strips

steps.text: Mix sour cream and lime juice together in a large bowl; season with salt and black pepper. Reserve about half the mixture in another bowl for serving.
Mince half the jalapeño pepper; save other half for later. Toss cabbage, green onions, and minced jalapeño half in remaining sour cream mixture until slaw is well mixed.
Heat olive oil and remaining jalapeño half in a large skillet over medium heat; swirl oil to coat skillet evenly. Season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper.
Pan-fry fish strips in the skillet in 2 batches until fish is golden brown and easily flaked with a fork, 5 to 6 minutes. Discard jalapeño half.
Heat tortillas in the microwave on high until warm, 20 to 30 seconds.
Serve fish in warmed tortillas topped with cabbage slaw, reserved sour cream mixture, and cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Fish Tacos
raw_recipe.description: Tilapia fillets are pan-fried in a jalapeno-infused oil and served with a quick cabbage slaw. For a milder flavor, remove the seeds from jalapeno peppers before adding to the slaw.

review.reviewBody:
This was excellent!! 
I made very minor changes: cooked the red cabbage in a pan for about 5 min, just to soften slightly. Used fat-free sour cream. Also, added cilantro to the slaw and as a garnish on top. I don't believe the recipe instructions included what to do with the cilantro.
This was the perfect dinner for a hot day!!

So good! I did not use any jalapeno while cooking but I plan to next time. Added one packet of sazon seasoning and some cumin to the fish while frying. Also pan fried fish inside the taco shells for crispy tacos using thin corn tortillas and sprinkled some cojita at the end. We already plan to have it again tonight.

This was really good! I made a few changes. I used non-fat yogurt instead of sour cream and seasoned the sauce with Spiceology Smoked Honey Habanero and Chili Margarite rubs instead of salt and pepper. Also added 1 T light mayo to the sauce. I cheated and used shredded cabbage mix. This was great with grilled tilapia seasoned with the same rubs I used in the sauce. Will definitely make again!

Increased to 1/2 Cup reduced fat sour cream. 

In food processor - Combined- Sour Cream, Cilantro, jalapeno (and jalapeno juice), ADDED hot sauce, and TxJOY steak seasoning (or any creole seasoning) to sauce for better flavor.

I made a few modifications to this recipe, to be specific, I used Crappie that I caught the same day instead of Talapia. I added Jalapeño sauce and Cayenne pepper dust to the slaw for some heat. Next time I might just use Cerrano peppers instead. I also used a 1/2 and 1/2 of Lime and Lemon juice in the Reduced Fat Sour Cream and let the slaw sit for 45 minutes in the fridge to allow the citric acid to soften the cabbage, which worked very very well. I used low-fat tortillas to help reduce the caloric intake as 2 just isn't enough in a serving. This is an amazing recipe with ultimate flexibility. I would suggest trying Non Fat Greek Yogurt in place of the Sour Cream and possibly corn tortillas in place of flour if you are truly on a stricter calorie intake.

So delicious! Made a few changes as per my preference. I zest the lime, and I only use 1Tbsp lime juice for the slaw. Half of the zest I put in the slaw, the other half in the reserved sour cream. I use 1/4 cup sour cream for the slaw and 1/4 for additional topping. Put the cilantro in the slaw to taste, then add on a bit to the tacos later. Only use white and light green parts of the green onions. I also love throwing some bread crumbs on the fish before cooking!
This was a delicious dish. I used broccoli coleslaw and softened it up before adding to the recipe. My family loved it and didn't realize it was a healthy dish. #winning.

I used Swai fillets (it was all I had); cut them into strips & baked them in a pan sprayed with cooking spray in a 425-degree (f) oven for 20 minutes or so. I sprayed the fillet pieces with cooking spray and sprinkled them with salt, pepper, dried cilantro, and chili powder, and put 1/2 the chopped jalapeno in with them as well. I stirred it around once as it baked. Otherwise, used green cabbage instead of red, and we topped them off with our favorite hot salsa. I was stunned that not only did my husband like it, but both our sons (20 and 22) actually liked it as well (they complain about fish, usually).

I had never made fish tacos before and my boys were very skeptical when they heard. However, we were very pleased with this recipe! Like some of the others, I sprinkled lime juice, salt, pepper, and garlic powder on the tilapia before I baked it in the oven at 400 for 8 minutes. I served additional "taco" toppings that each person individually added. It was easy to prepare, felt fresh, and tasted great!

Family loved it! I basically doubled the whole thing, used plenty of lime, salt, pepper, and 1 bag of regular slaw. I did pre-fry the slaw for a few minutes to soften it as someone else suggested which worked great. I just folded all the sour cream mixture right into the slaw. For us, we could have used a little more kick/seasoning on the fish and in the slaw which I'll add next time. Definitely a winner though!

This dish really is quick and tasty! 

I did make a few substitutions. I switched flour tortillas for corn tortillas, which really gave it the restaurant taste. I also didn't use the jalapeno because I foolishly made it for the kids also - who are super picky (1 and 4 yrs). 

I topped it with fresh tomatoes and a yummy cilantro lime salsa from Aldi.

All of my ingredients were purchased from Trader Joe's, which I swear is one of the best spots for quality ingredients. 

I will most certainly be making this again!
I am not sure if I cooked the fish long enough to make it more golden. Family was split on this recipe.

Made this for couples game night. Everyone really enjoyed it! Super easy recipe. Quick create. The only change I made was I used pre-breaded cod filets from Costco. We do love the crispy crunch of a good fish taco! Will be using this recipe again.

Quick and Easy!

Big Hit last Taco Tuesday so we're doing it again!!!
I just made this for dinner tonight, and it was so delicious!! It was super easy, quick to make, pretty inexpensive, and my family loved it. I’ll definitely add this in the meal rotation!
First time making them and they are definitely delicious
I have made this recipe a few times! It’s excellent and the only major changes I make are adding more hot spices and peppers in. It’s a fantastic recipe the way it is though too.
I followed the recipe exactly except I added cilantro to the slaw mixture as other reviewers suggested. Sooo good! We’ve made them four times in the past two weeks!!!

This was excellent!!!! Used coleslaw mixed cabbage. Great way to cook up some largemouth bass. I do soak the bass in milk for a couple hours. I feel it helps elongate the fishy taste of bass. Will make this again!
